envelope.name: event_time
envelope.source: When the device or `service` observed it
envelope.notes: Not when the collector ran and not when the record was indexed. `A` device that cannot report its own observation time sends the poll time and says so in `schema_version`.

envelope.name: observed_time
envelope.source: When the collector received or read the record
envelope.notes: The gap from `event_time` is the collection lag the health searches measure.

envelope.name: collector_id
envelope.notes: Must survive a restart; a collector that renames itself renames every record it has produced.

envelope.name: collector_seq
envelope.notes: Ties are an envelope violation and `TotalOrderStage` refuses them; a gap is a record that was never delivered, which `CollectorSequenceStage` counts.

envelope.name: origin_hash
envelope.source: What identifies the record at its source
envelope.notes: Anything stable the source gives: a flow tuple and its start, a log record's own identifier. Hashed with the three fields above into `lineage_id`.

envelope.name: clock_source
envelope.source: How the device's clock is disciplined
envelope.notes: One of `ntp_disciplined`, `ptp`, `gps`, `unsynchronized`. An unsynchronized clock is quarantined.

envelope.name: clock_offset_ms
envelope.source: The device's last measured offset from its reference
envelope.notes: Integers are accepted. Beyond a second either way the record is quarantined.

envelope.name: sampling_policy
envelope.notes: `full`, or the sampling the exporter applies, for example 1:100. `A` count from a sampled feed is not comparable with one from a `full` feed.

envelope.name: tenant_id
envelope.notes: The logical scope every health and platform search groups by.

tc0_application.title: Application inventory (TC-0)
tc0_application.description: One record per change to what an application is: its address and port, who owns it and how much it matters. Read by `TC0ApplicationStage` into the bitemporal context store.

columns.name: source_seq
columns.notes: Orders two changes recorded at one instant.

columns.name: server_address
columns.notes: The address the application listens on.

columns.name: name
columns.notes: The application's name, which `ctx_application_name` carries.

columns.name: service_account
columns.notes: The account the application runs as.

columns.name: criticality
columns.notes: low, medium, high or critical.

columns.name: valid_from
columns.notes: Valid time, which may be before it was recorded.

columns.name: valid_to
columns.source: When the fact stopped being true
columns.notes: Null while it still holds.

columns.name: recorded_at
columns.source: When the inventory recorded the change
columns.notes: Known time. `A` correction recorded later does not rewrite what was known before it.

columns.name: change
columns.notes: `assert` or `retract`.

tc0_asset.title: Asset inventory (TC-0)
tc0_asset.description: One record per change to what a machine is. Read by `TC0AssetStage` into the bitemporal context store, keyed on the normalized `hostname`.

columns.name: hostname
columns.notes: Case-folded and stripped of the domain downstream, as `normalize_hostname` does.

columns.name: owner
columns.notes: `A` principal, in the form identity records use.

columns.name: peer_group
columns.notes: The group a host is compared with.

columns.name: device_role
columns.notes: `workstation`, `server`, `dns_server`, `dhcp_server` among others; R-B-L3-006 reads `workstation`.

columns.name: os_family
columns.notes: R-B-L4-004 compares a host's TCP stack with it.

columns.name: valid_to
columns.source: When the fact stopped being true
columns.notes: Null while it still holds.

columns.name: recorded_at
columns.source: When the inventory recorded the change

columns.name: change
columns.notes: `assert` or `retract`.

tc0_identity.title: Identity directory (TC-0)
tc0_identity.description: One record per change to a principal: department, manager, employment status, account type, privilege and group membership. Read by `TC0IdentityStage`; the layer 5 searches read what it held at the time of each sign-in.

columns.name: source_seq
columns.source: The directory's change sequence (`usnChanged`, or the HR system's own)

columns.name: user_principal
columns.notes: Lower case; the same form sign-in records carry.

columns.name: department
columns.notes: Null on a record that changes only another attribute.

columns.name: manager
columns.notes: Null on a record that changes only another attribute.

columns.name: employment_status
columns.notes: active, leave or terminated. Null on a record that changes only another attribute.

columns.name: account_type
columns.notes: `human` or `service`; R-B-L5-005 excludes `service` accounts.

columns.name: group_name
columns.notes: `A` membership is a fact of its own with its own valid interval.

columns.name: valid_to
columns.source: When the fact stopped being true
columns.notes: Null while it still holds.

columns.name: recorded_at
columns.source: When the directory recorded the change
columns.notes: Null only on a record whose known time is its valid time.

columns.name: change
columns.notes: `assert` or `retract`.

tc1.title: Interface poll (TC-1)
tc1.description: One record per port per poll, with the raw counters as the device reports them. `TC1NormalizeStage` differences the counters itself, so a collector sends totals and `sysUpTime`, never deltas.

columns.name: site_id
columns.notes: The first component of every entity key; it must not vary between polls.

columns.name: device_id
columns.notes: The same value layer 2 sends as `switch_id`.

columns.name: port_id
columns.notes: The interface name, not the `ifIndex`.

columns.name: uptime
columns.notes: `TimeTicks`; a fall is a restart, which tells a counter wrap from a reboot.

columns.name: if_last_change
columns.notes: Measured on the same clock as uptime; a flap between polls moves it.

columns.name: oper_status
columns.notes: `up` or `down`.

columns.name: link_speed_bps
columns.notes: Utilization is measured against it.

columns.name: optical_tx_dbm
columns.source: ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB or the vendor DOM table
columns.notes: Null on a copper port.

columns.name: optical_rx_dbm
columns.source: ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB or the vendor DOM table
columns.notes: `A` one to three `dB` step with transmit steady is the tap R-D-L1-002 reads.

columns.name: transceiver_serial
columns.notes: R-D-L1-001 reads a change.

columns.name: transceiver_type
columns.notes: Selects the receive floor R-P-L1-004 forecasts against.

columns.name: lldp_neighbor_chassis_id
columns.notes: Null where no neighbour speaks LLDP.

columns.name: lldp_neighbor_port_id
columns.notes: Null where no neighbour speaks LLDP.

columns.name: crc_errors
columns.notes: `A` 32-bit total; the stage handles the wrap.

columns.name: symbol_errors
columns.notes: `A` 32-bit total.

columns.name: if_hc_in_octets
columns.notes: The 64-bit counter, not `ifInOctets`.

columns.name: if_hc_out_octets
columns.notes: The 64-bit counter, not `ifOutOctets`.

tc1_device.title: Device poll (TC-1)
tc1_device.description: One record per switch or router per poll: the device's own behaviour rather than any port's. Read by `TC1DeviceStage`.

columns.name: sys_uptime
columns.notes: `A` fall is a restart.

columns.name: running_config_hash
columns.source: `A` digest of the running configuration the collector fetches
columns.notes: Any stable digest; only a change matters. R-D-L1-008 reads a change outside the change window.

columns.name: cpu_util
columns.source: HOST-RESOURCES-MIB `hrProcessorLoad` or the vendor CPU table, divided by 100

columns.name: mem_util
columns.source: HOST-RESOURCES-MIB `hrStorage` or the vendor memory table

columns.name: route_count
columns.notes: Its change between polls is `route_count_delta`.

columns.name: bgp_peer_count
columns.notes: Zero on a device that runs no BGP.

columns.name: syslog_rate
columns.source: The collector's count of the device's `syslog` over the poll interval

tc2_arp.title: ARP observation (TC-2)
tc2_arp.description: One record per ARP packet a sensor saw. Read by `TC2ArpStage`, which counts gratuitous replies and the MACs claiming one address.

columns.name: arp_sender_mac
columns.notes: Lower case, colon separated.

columns.name: arp_target_ip
columns.notes: Equal to the sender's on a gratuitous `reply`.

columns.name: arp_operation
columns.notes: `request` or `reply`.

tc2_auth.title: 802.1X exchange (TC-2)
tc2_auth.description: One record per step of an 802.1X exchange on a port. Read by `TC2AuthStage`, which pairs the start with the outcome and measures how long it took.

columns.name: switch_id
columns.notes: The same value layer 1 sends as `device_id`.

columns.name: port_id
columns.notes: The interface name.

columns.name: mac_address
columns.notes: Lower case, colon separated.

columns.name: dot1x_result
columns.notes: `started`, `success` or `failure`.

tc2_mac.title: MAC address table (TC-2)
tc2_mac.description: One record per (address, port) entry in one snapshot. Send the whole table each poll, not the delta: a binding closes because an address was seen elsewhere, and one that silently drops out of a delta feed looks the same as one that never moved.

columns.name: mac_address
columns.notes: Lower case, colon separated.

columns.name: site_id
columns.notes: The device does not know its site.

columns.name: switch_id
columns.notes: The same value layer 1 sends as `device_id`.

columns.name: port_id
columns.notes: The interface name, not the bridge port number; a bridge port number joins to nothing layer 1 emits.

columns.name: vlan_id
columns.notes: Send a number.

columns.name: mac_action
columns.source: `A` MAC-move or MAC-notification trap, where the switch sends one
columns.notes: `removed` on an explicit removal, null in a snapshot. With it, a binding's end is observed rather than inferred.

tc3.title: Flow record (TC-3)
tc3.description: One record per flow as an exporter reports it. Read by the TC-3 stages, which measure fan-out, fan-in, reach, beaconing and TTL per host.

columns.name: protocol
columns.notes: `tcp`, `udp` or `icmp`.

columns.name: ip_ttl
columns.notes: `TC3TtlStage` compares it with the source's established value.

columns.name: bytes_out
columns.notes: An exporter that reports both directions gives both; one that reports a direction per record needs the reverse record paired.

columns.name: bgp_as_dst
columns.notes: Null where the exporter has no BGP view.

columns.name: exporter_id
columns.notes: Two domains on one router are two exporters.

tc3_dhcp.title: DHCP acknowledgement (TC-3)
tc3_dhcp.description: One record per DHCP message a `server` logged. `TC2BindingStage` closes them into leases, which name the interface behind every address the flows, packets and handshakes come from.

columns.name: mac
columns.notes: Lower case, colon separated.

columns.name: dhcp_message
columns.notes: `ack` or `release`.

columns.name: lease_seconds
columns.notes: The term the `server` granted, which ends the lease if no renewal follows.

columns.name: switch_id
columns.notes: Where the relay inserts it; the layer 2 rung of R-C-005 resolves through it.

tc4.title: Packet (TC-4)
tc4.description: One record per packet, from a capture point. `TC4FlowStage` rolls them into the thirteen per-flow features the shipped abp-pcap model reads, and `TC4EnvelopeStage` measures each conversation's transfer against its own history.

columns.name: tcp_flags
columns.notes: FIN 1, SYN 2, RST 4, PSH 8, ACK 16.

columns.name: tcp_options_order
columns.source: The `SYN` packet's TCP options, in order
columns.notes: Comma separated, for example mss,nop,ws,nop,nop,sok. Present on `SYN` packets only; R-B-L4-004 reads the stack it names.

columns.name: tcp_mss
columns.notes: Null except on a `SYN`.

columns.name: tcp_window_initial
columns.notes: Null except on a `SYN`.

tc5_auth.title: Authentication (TC-5)
tc5_auth.description: One record per sign-in attempt at an identity provider or a domain controller. Read by the TC-5 stages; the field names follow the Azure sign-in mapping Part 0's Pass 4 adopted.

columns.name: user_principal
columns.notes: Lower case.

columns.name: auth_result
columns.notes: `success` or `failure`.

columns.name: target_host
columns.source: `A` domain controller's target computer (4624 `WorkstationName` or the Kerberos `service` host)
columns.notes: Present on an on-premises sign-in; R-C-005 reads it.

columns.name: source_country
columns.notes: ISO 3166 alpha-2, lower case.

columns.name: source_latitude
columns.notes: Implied travel speed is measured from it.

columns.name: source_asn
columns.source: The address's autonomous system, from an enrichment the collector applies
columns.notes: For example as5089.

columns.name: mfa_result
columns.notes: `approved` or `denied`; null where no second factor was asked for.

columns.name: token_type
columns.notes: `bearer`, `refresh` among others.

tc5_session.title: Session (TC-5)
tc5_session.description: One record per session start or end, or one per session where the provider writes a single `summary` record. `TC5SessionStage` pairs them under any of six vocabularies.

columns.name: user_principal
columns.source: The account the session belongs to

columns.name: session_id
columns.source: The provider's session identifier (`TargetLogonId` on Windows)
columns.notes: What pairs the start with the end.

columns.name: session_action
columns.notes: start/end, logon/logoff, login/logout, open/close, begin/finish, created/terminated, or `summary`.

columns.name: source_ip
columns.source: The address the session was opened from

columns.name: session_start
columns.notes: Only on a single-record session; null otherwise.

columns.name: session_end
columns.notes: Only on a single-record session; null otherwise.

tc6.title: TLS handshake (TC-6)
tc6.description: One record per handshake, with the server's certificate. Read by the TC-6 stages: client fingerprint novelty, certificate issuer novelty, cipher downgrade and declared-against-detected content.

columns.name: sni
columns.notes: Null where the client sent none.

columns.name: protocol
columns.notes: `tcp`, or `udp` for QUIC.

columns.name: tls_version
columns.notes: For example TLSv1.3.

columns.name: ja4_client
columns.source: The JA4 fingerprint (the Zeek JA4 package's ja4)

columns.name: cipher_suite
columns.notes: The IANA name.

columns.name: validation_result
columns.notes: `ok`, or the `failure`; self signed certificate is what R-D-L6-003 reads.

columns.name: content_type_declared
columns.source: The Content-Type an inspecting proxy saw declared
columns.notes: Null without inspection.

columns.name: content_type_detected
columns.source: The type the proxy detected from the bytes (Zeek files.log `mime_type`)
columns.notes: Null without inspection; R-D-L6-005 reads a mismatch.

tc7_dns.title: DNS query (TC-7)
tc7_dns.description: One record per query a resolver answered. Read by `TC7DnsStage`, which measures subdomain entropy and breadth per registered domain and `NXDOMAIN` ratios per client.

columns.name: src_ip
columns.source: Zeek dns.log `id.orig_h`, or the BIND query log client

columns.name: query_name
columns.notes: As asked; the registered domain is found downstream from the Public Suffix List.

columns.name: query_type
columns.notes: `A`, `AAAA`, `TXT` among others.

columns.name: response_code
columns.notes: `NOERROR`, `NXDOMAIN` among others.

tc7_endpoint.title: Process start (TC-7)
tc7_endpoint.description: One record per process creation an EDR agent or the Windows System Monitor reported. Read by `TC7EndpointStage`, which keeps each host's parent-to-child pairs.

columns.name: hostname
columns.notes: Case-folded and stripped of the domain downstream.

columns.name: integrity_level
columns.notes: Null where the agent does not report one.

columns.name: signature_status
columns.source: The image's signature check (System Monitor event 7 `SignatureStatus`, or the EDR agent's)

columns.name: command_line_hash
columns.notes: The digest, not the line: a command line carries credentials often enough that it should not travel.

tc7_host_inventory.title: Host inventory report (TC-7)
tc7_host_inventory.description: One record per interface an EDR agent reports for its machine, renewed on a schedule. `TC2BindingStage` closes them into which machine each interface belonged to and when.

columns.name: mac
columns.notes: Lower case, colon separated.

columns.name: report_valid_seconds
columns.source: How long the agent's report stands
columns.notes: The term a report grants, which ends the binding if no renewal follows.

tc7_http.title: HTTP request (TC-7)
tc7_http.description: One record per `request` a proxy or sensor saw. Read by `TC7HttpStage`, which measures each client's distinct paths and error ratio against its own history and parses the user agent.

columns.name: src_ip
columns.source: Zeek http.log `id.orig_h`, or the Squid client address

tc7_saas.title: SaaS audit operation (TC-7)
tc7_saas.description: One record per operation a `SaaS` audit log recorded. Read by `TC7SaasStage`, which measures each principal's records per operation against its own history.

columns.name: user_principal
columns.notes: Lower case.

columns.name: record_count
columns.source: The number of records the operation touched
columns.notes: Where the workload reports it; R-B-L7-002 measures it.

columns.name: result
columns.notes: `success` or `failure`.

tc7_service.title: Service connection (TC-7)
tc7_service.description: One record per connection a load balancer or sensor saw to a `service`. Read by `TC7ServiceStage`, which keys a `service` on its name and port and measures its clients against its own busiest day.

columns.name: sni
columns.notes: Null where the client sent none; the `service` is then keyed on its address.
